create.name: Sal Worringham
create.bio:
Sal Worringham teaches yoga and meditation from The Willow Clinic, a pair of treatment and practice rooms at the bottom of her garden in the Surrey village of Wonersh, near Guildford, and online over Zoom. She has kept a daily sadhana of yoga, breathwork, mantra, meditation and study for around thirty years and has led meditation groups for more than twenty-five of them. Her yoga training is in the Akhanda tradition, completed partly in London and partly at Anand Prakash Ashram in Rishikesh, with further hours in yin and hatha yoga.

Her weekly Akhanda yoga classes, one in a village hall and one live online, combine postures, pranayama, philosophy themes, mantra, meditation and relaxation, and are open to all ages, with chair options. Her meditation groups, several each week in person and a fortnightly session on Zoom, are run as a small sangha: guided practice, unscripted and led in the moment, followed by gentle shared enquiry into what is arising. She has studied Compassionate Inquiry with Gabor Maté and attended workshops with Tara Brach and Jack Kornfield. The group also gathers for equinox and solstice rituals, outings such as meditation and drumming at Glastonbury Tor, and a residential retreat.

courses.title: Meditation Groups
courses.description: Small weekly and fortnightly meditation groups at The Willow Clinic in Wonersh, plus a fortnightly live session on Zoom that is also recorded. Each meets as a community for guided meditation and gentle shared enquiry into present experience.

courses.title: Akhanda Yoga Classes
courses.description: A Saturday morning class in Blackheath Village Hall near Guildford and a Monday afternoon class live on Zoom, with recordings available for a week. Classes weave postures, breathwork, a philosophy theme, mantra, meditation and relaxation, and chair options are offered.

courses.title: The Story Keeper Women's Retreat
courses.description: A residential weekend for women at Florence House in East Sussex, the group's fourth retreat there. Earlier retreats in this setting combined meditation, yoga, breathwork, affirmation work and fire ceremonies.
